metadata.title: Original-Row Proximal Splitting for Side-Specific and Directional Peak Penalties: Two Negative Timing Studies
metadata.description:
Original-row proximal updates can represent selected soft interval penalties without adding explicit departure variables to a quadratic program's principal system. We derive a side-specific separable linear-quadratic update and a directional disjoint group-peak update in a fixed positive diagonal metric. The grouped construction follows a box-residual identity under coordinate contractions and reduces its proximal operation to a weighted scalar threshold. Exact lifting, directional row splitting and compact epigraphs already express the same objectives; no expressibility or algorithmic-priority claim is made. We evaluate the two implementations in separate registered synthetic studies. The first contains 456 instances and 168 held-out accepted pairs: median relative cold end-to-end reduction 0.499839%, with 95% seed-cluster limits -3.291967% and 3.944835%. The second contains 210 repeated-forecast instances, with a 144-member held-out primary score of -212.449875%, limits -225.336618% and -192.873759%, and 9 retained failed pairs. Neither predicted ten-percent timing improvement is established. Original-space objective, hard-row and dual checks distinguish mathematical equivalence from computational cost. Matched formulation, conditioning and workspace comparisons quantify descriptive contrasts without asserting an unperformed causal ablation. The results show that fewer principal variables or rows do not by themselves establish a faster complete optimization operation on these tested populations.

Editable LaTeX sources and code: CAOS_SoftQP. Native engine: CAOS_SoftQP_Engine. Complete grouped evidence: dataset.
metadata.version_notes: Corrected native research preprint. Clarifies hard-row indicator terms, the registered acceptance checks and paired descriptive contrasts. Both registered timing conclusions remain negative.
